benefit.what_is_claimed: That AI makes drug discovery faster and more successful overall. What has been measured is lower Phase I attrition; no advantage in Phase II efficacy has been shown. Secondary reviews found that the FDA had approved no AI-discovered drug as of July 2026, and no later approval was found.
benefit.what_is_measured: The first published analysis of the pipelines of AI-native biotech companies appeared in Drug Discovery Today (online 30 April 2024, by BCG authors). It found that AI-discovered molecules succeeded in Phase I 80 to 90% of the time, well above historic industry averages. In Phase II the rate was about 40%, on a limited sample, which is comparable to historic averages. Secondary reports of the paper's body give 75 AI-derived molecules entering the clinic since 2015, and 67 in clinical trials in 2023. Among computationally designed molecules, zasocitinib (TAK-279) is at the application stage. It is a TYK2 inhibitor that Nimbus Therapeutics designed with Schrödinger's physics-based FEP+ simulations. On 14 September 2026 Takeda announced that the FDA had accepted its NDA for plaque psoriasis under Priority Review, with a target action date in the first quarter of 2027.

benefit.title: AI-supported mammography was non-inferior to double reading on interval cancers in a trial of 105,934 women
benefit.what_is_claimed: That AI makes breast screening both better and cheaper everywhere. The 12% lower interval-cancer rate was not statistically significant, and the trial was designed to show non-inferiority. It tested one AI system in one national programme and has not reported mortality.
benefit.what_is_measured: MASAI randomised 105,934 women in Sweden between 12 April 2021 and 7 December 2022. One arm had AI-supported screening, in which AI sent each exam to single or double reading and supported detection; the other had standard double reading (The Lancet, 29 January 2026; 105,915 analysed). Interval cancers were 1.55 per 1,000 in the AI arm (82 of 53,043) and 1.76 per 1,000 in the control arm (93 of 52,872). The proportion ratio was 0.88 (95% CI 0.65 to 1.18), which met the 20% non-inferiority margin. Sensitivity was 80.5% vs 73.8%, and specificity was 98.5% in both arms. An earlier report from the same trial found 29% more cancers detected (6.4 vs 5.0 per 1,000) and 44.2% fewer screen readings, with no significant rise in false positives.

benefit.what_is_measured: DeepMind reported on 14 May 2025 that its Gemini-powered search agent found a way to multiply 4x4 complex-valued matrices with 48 scalar multiplications. benefit.what_is_claimed: That intelligence is becoming 'too cheap to meter'. These are falling list prices at fixed capability for the cheapest qualifying model. They are not total spending or energy use, and not the price of frontier capability.
benefit.what_is_measured: Epoch AI (22 September 2026) finds that across five benchmarks the cost of reaching a given level of performance has fallen about 47% per quarter since 2023, or 13x per year. Its example is 75% on GPQA Diamond: about $0.30 per question with OpenAI's o3 in early 2025, against $0.0004 with GPT-5.6 Luna just under 18 months later, a 725-fold drop. harm.what_is_measured: Anthropic's 10 September 2026 report covers operations it disrupted between December 2025 and August 2026. A Russian espionage actor (GTG-20006; Anthropic says its attribution is consistent with public reporting on Midnight Blizzard) 'used AI at every point in their operations'. One of its intrusions, against a North African government technology authority, took more than 300,000 national identity records and registry data on more than half a million companies. A suspected ShinyHunters affiliate breached a SaaS provider and took data belonging to roughly 200 of its customer organisations. The same affiliate then dumped over 2,100 Azure AD token sets from more than 40 corporate tenants in about 34 hours. A single French-speaking hacktivist targeted 42 entities, got internal access to at least 14, and took an estimated 12–26 GB, including political donor records.

harm.caveat: Editors curate the entries from press reports, and many are allegations ('Reportedly', 'Allegedly' in the titles). IDs are assigned when an incident is processed, often long after the event, so additions per period show editorial throughput, not how often harms occur. The count of 1,703 comes from the site's GraphQL endpoint, which accepts only requests carrying the site's own origin and is not documented as a public API. The incident pages themselves are public.

harm.caveat: The monitor detects events automatically from news. It merges incidents (harm occurred) with hazards (harm could occur), and one event can draw many articles. It measures media coverage, not verified harm, and its per-event summaries and incident/hazard classifications are labelled '[AI generated]'. The total is the figure the page shows for its default search. The OECD says the monitor should not be reported as representing official OECD views.

It says 182,000+ involved offenders possessing, generating or attempting to generate AI CSAM. That total is made up of 7,000+ reports of generating or possessing, 30,000+ of attempting to generate by uploading a file with text prompts, and 145,000+ of using AI to engage with or alter an existing CSAM file. A further 12,000+ were CSAM that companies found in AI training data, 3,000+ involved other uses such as chat-based exploitation, and 200,000+ had an AI link without enough detail to classify. harm.title: FCC fines Steve Kramer $6M for 9,581 deepfake Biden robocalls sent before the NH primary
harm.what_is_measured: The FCC found that on 2024-01-21, two days before the New Hampshire primary, calls Kramer commissioned went out with an AI voice clone of President Biden and a spoofed caller ID. Voice Broadcasting initiated 9,581 of them. The FCC adopted a $6,000,000 forfeiture on 2024-09-26 (released 2024-09-30). It set $1,000 for each of 3,000 verified calls and doubled the total for egregiousness. Kramer did not respond to the proposed fine. The originating carrier, Lingo Telecom, paid $1,000,000.

harm.what_is_measured: The FTC's complaint says Rite Aid used AI facial recognition in hundreds of stores from 2012 to 2020 and that it generated 'thousands of false-positive matches'. harm.title: Wrongful-death suits over teen suicides: Character.AI and Google settled; the Raine v. OpenAI case continues
harm.what_is_measured: Garcia v. Character Technologies (M.D. Fla. 6:24-cv-01903) was filed on 2024-10-22 over the death of 14-year-old Sewell Setzer III. On 2025-05-20 the court granted in part and denied in part the defendants' motions to dismiss. On 2026-01-07 Character Technologies filed a Notice of Resolution, and the court dismissed the case without prejudice pending a stipulated final order. That deadline was extended on 2026-04-09 (by 120 days) and again on 2026-08-04 (by 90 days). CNN reported that the agreement covers Character.AI, its founders and Google, as well as four other cases. Raine v. OpenAI (SF Superior Court CGC-25-628528) concerns 16-year-old Adam Raine. In its 2025-11-25 answer, OpenAI says ChatGPT directed him to crisis resources or trusted people 'more than 100 times' and that his death 'was not caused by ChatGPT'. No resolution of Raine has been reported.

harm.title: UN Panel on Libya documents deployment of the Kargu-2, which it calls a lethal autonomous weapons system (2020)
harm.what_is_claimed: The first time a killer robot autonomously hunted and killed humans.
harm.what_is_measured: The UN Panel of Experts report S/2021/229 (8 March 2021, para. 63) covers the period after Operation PEACE STORM began on 27 March 2020. It says logistics convoys and retreating HAF forces 'were subsequently hunted down and remotely engaged' by drones 'or' lethal autonomous weapons such as the STM Kargu-2. It says these were 'programmed to attack targets without requiring data connectivity between the operator and the munition'. The Panel's table records a Kargu-2 transfer from Turkey, identified on 27 May 2020. This documents that the system was deployed; the report attributes no casualties to autonomous engagement.

honesty: No net score. The two registers are never summed, subtracted or weighed against each other. A fraud loss in dollars, a lung-function change in millilitres and a count of mapped cameras share no unit, and any exchange rate between them would be a value judgement dressed as arithmetic.
Every figure is taken from a linked source, and every number carries its own source and date. Where sources disagree, the caveat says so. Nothing is estimated.
Curated by hand and dated, not live. Each row was checked against its sources on its as_of date. The live counts are in data/balance.json, which is fetched; this file is not.
Each row records the claim beside the measurement so a reader can see the gap between them. Recording a claim is not endorsing it.
The number of rows on each side is a choice made by the compilers, not a measurement. Equal lengths are not a finding that the two sides are equal, and unequal lengths would not be a finding either.
A status word describes the evidence, not the importance. No status on one side ranks a row against any row on the other.
The verification pass of 2026-09-28 dropped no row outright. dropped[] lists what individual rows left out, and why.

benefit.claimed: asserted by the organisation behind it with no measurement a stranger can check; listed so the claim is visible, never counted as a benefit
benefit.delivered: the output exists at scale and a stranger can check it: a database, a dataset, an authorisation list, a price
benefit.demonstrated: shown to work in a study, a trial or a test, and not documented as in routine use
benefit.in-trial: in human clinical trials; no approval, and no outcome beyond what the trials have reported
benefit.in-use: deployed and working for people outside the organisation that built it, by the operator's own report

harm.alleged: charged in a complaint or a lawsuit and not adjudicated; the allegation is the record, not a finding
harm.documented: a specific event recorded in an official finding, a court record or a named organisation's own report
harm.measured: a count or a rate from a published dataset or study, with its denominator and its method

what_this_is: Two registers kept side by side: what AI has measurably delivered or demonstrated, and what harm it has been documented, measured or alleged to cause. Each row separates what was measured from what is claimed about it, with the sources for both.
